Verses 20-21, which were missing, have been restored.

verses.text: It was the 3rd year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah. Then Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, and besieged (attacked) it.

And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into Nebuchadnezzar's hand. He also gave part of the vessels (cups and bowls) of the house of God. Nebuchadnezzar carried them into the land of Shinar, to the house of his god. He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.

And the king spoke to Ashpenaz, the master of his eunuchs (palace officials). He told Ashpenaz to bring certain of the children of Israel. They were to be of the king's seed (family), and of the princes (nobles).

They were to be children in whom was no blemish (flaw). They were to be well favoured (good looking), and skilful in all wisdom. They were to be cunning (wise) in knowledge, and understanding science. They were to have ability to stand in the king's palace. And they were to be taught the learning and the tongue (language) of the Chaldeans.

And the king appointed them a daily provision (portion) of the king's meat (food). He also gave them the wine which he drank. So he would nourish (feed) them 3 years. At the end of that time they would stand before the king.
Now among these were some of the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

The prince of the eunuchs (chief palace official) gave them names. He gave to Daniel the name of Belteshazzar. To Hananiah he gave the name of Shadrach. To Mishael he gave the name of Meshach. And to Azariah he gave the name of Abednego.

But Daniel purposed in his heart (firmly decided) that he would not defile (make unclean) himself. He would not eat the portion of the king's meat (food). Nor would he drink the wine which the king drank. So Daniel asked the prince of the eunuchs not to make him unclean.
Now God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love. It was with the prince of the eunuchs (chief palace official).

And the prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel: I fear my lord the king. He has appointed your meat (food) and your drink. Why should he see your faces worse liking (looking worse)? They would look worse than the children of your age. Then you would make me endanger my head to the king.
Then Daniel spoke to Melzar. The prince of the eunuchs had set Melzar over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
Daniel said: Prove (test) your servants, I beseech (beg) you, 10 days. Let them give us pulse (vegetables) to eat, and water to drink.
Then let our countenances (faces) be looked upon before you. Look at the faces of the children that eat the king's meat (food). And as you see, deal with your servants.
So Melzar consented (agreed) to them in this matter, and proved (tested) them 10 days.
At the end of 10 days their countenances (faces) appeared fairer (looked better). They were fatter in flesh (healthier) than all the other children. Those children ate the king's meat (food).
So Melzar took away the portion of their meat (food). He took away the wine that they should drink. And he gave them pulse (vegetables).
As for these 4 children, God gave them knowledge and skill. He gave them skill in all learning and wisdom. And Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
Now the end of the days came that the king had set. Then the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king communed (talked) with them. Among them all was found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Therefore they stood before the king.
The king enquired (asked) of them in all matters of wisdom and understanding. He found them 10 times better than all the magicians and astrologers. They were better than all in his realm (kingdom).
And Daniel continued even to the first year of king Cyrus.

verses.text: In the 2nd year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams. His spirit was troubled, and his sleep broke from him.

Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the astrologers. He also called the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans (wise men of Babylon). They were to show the king his dreams. So they came and stood before the king.
And the king said to them: I have dreamed a dream. My spirit was troubled to know the dream.
Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Syriack (the Aramaic language): O king, live for ever. Tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation (meaning).

The king answered and said to the Chaldeans: The thing is gone from me. You must make known to me the dream, with the interpretation (meaning) of it. If you will not, you shall be cut in pieces. And your houses shall be made a dunghill (garbage heap).

But you may show the dream, and the interpretation (meaning) of it. Then you shall receive gifts and rewards and great honour from me. Therefore show me the dream, and the interpretation (meaning) of it.
They answered again and said: Let the king tell his servants the dream. And we will show the interpretation (meaning) of it.
The king answered and said: I know of certainty (for sure) that you would gain the time (stall for time). You do this because you see the thing is gone from me.

You may not make known to me the dream. Then there is but one decree (law) for you. For you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me. You hope the time will be changed. Therefore tell me the dream. Then I shall know that you can show me the interpretation (meaning) of it.

The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said: There is not a man upon the earth that can show the king's matter. Therefore no king, lord, nor ruler asked such things. No one asked it of any magician, or astrologer, or Chaldean.
And it is a rare (hard) thing that the king requires. There is no other that can show it before the king, except the gods. And their dwelling (home) is not with flesh (people).
For this cause the king was angry and very furious. And he commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
And the decree (law) went forth (out) that the wise men should be slain (killed). And they sought (looked for) Daniel and his fellows (friends) to be slain (killed).
Then Daniel answered with counsel and wisdom to Arioch. Arioch was the captain of the king's guard. He was gone forth (out) to slay (kill) the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel answered and said to Arioch the king's captain: Why is the decree (law) so hasty (quick) from the king? Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.
Then Daniel went in, and desired (asked) of the king to give him time. Then Daniel would show the king the interpretation (meaning).
Then Daniel went to his house. He made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions (friends).

They were to desire mercies (ask for mercy) of the God of heaven concerning this secret. That way Daniel and his fellows (friends) should not perish (die). They would not die with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then was the secret revealed (shown) to Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel answered and said: Blessed be the name of God for ever and ever. For wisdom and might are His.
And He changes the times and the seasons. He removes kings, and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who know understanding.
He reveals (shows) the deep and secret things. He knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells (lives) with Him.

I thank You, and praise You, O God of my fathers. You have given me wisdom and might. You have made known to me now what we desired (asked) of You. For You have now made known to us the king's matter.

Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch. The king had ordained (appointed) Arioch to destroy the wise men of Babylon. Daniel went and said this to Arioch: Destroy not the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king. And I will show the king the interpretation (meaning).

Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste (a hurry). Arioch said this to the king: I have found a man of the captives (prisoners) of Judah. He will make known to the king the interpretation (meaning).
The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar: Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen? Can you tell me the interpretation (meaning) of it?

Daniel answered in the presence of the king, and said: The wise men cannot show the secret which the king has demanded. Neither can the astrologers, the magicians, nor the soothsayers (fortune tellers).

But there is a God in heaven that reveals (shows) secrets. He makes known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head upon your bed, are these:

As for you, O king, your thoughts came into your mind upon your bed. You thought about what should come to pass (happen) hereafter (in the future). And He that reveals (shows) secrets makes known to you what shall happen.

But as for me, this secret is not revealed (shown) for my wisdom. I do not have more wisdom than any living. It is revealed for those who make known the interpretation (meaning) to the king. It is so that you might know the thoughts of your heart.
You, O king, saw, and look, a great image (statue). This great image, whose brightness was excellent, stood before you. And the form of it was terrible (frightening).
This image's (statue's) head was of fine gold. Its breast and its arms were of silver. Its belly and its thighs were of brass (bronze).
Its legs were of iron. Its feet were part of iron and part of clay.
You saw till a stone was cut out without hands. The stone smote (struck) the image (statue) upon its feet that were of iron and clay. And it brake (broke) them to pieces.

Then the iron, the clay, and the brass (bronze) were broken together. The silver and the gold were broken too. They became like the chaff (husks) of the summer threshingfloors. And the wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them. And the stone that smote (struck) the image became a great mountain. It filled the whole earth.
This is the dream. And we will tell the interpretation (meaning) of it before the king.
You, O king, are a king of kings. For the God of heaven has given you a kingdom. He gave you power, and strength, and glory.

The children of men dwell (live) in many places. Wherever they dwell, He has given them into your hand. He has given you the beasts (animals) of the field. He gave you the fowls (birds) of the heaven. He has made you ruler over them all. You are this head of gold.
And after you shall arise another kingdom inferior (lower) to you. And another third kingdom of brass (bronze) shall bear rule over all the earth.
And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron. For iron breaks in pieces and subdues (beats down) all things. As iron breaks all these, so shall it break in pieces and bruise (crush).

You saw the feet and toes, part of potters' clay, and part of iron. So the kingdom shall be divided. But there shall be in it of the strength of the iron. For you saw the iron mixed with miry (muddy) clay.
And the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay. So the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.

And you saw iron mixed with miry (muddy) clay. So they shall mingle (mix) themselves with the seed (children) of men. But they shall not cleave (stick) one to another. It is even as iron is not mixed with clay.

In the days of these kings, God shall set up a kingdom. He is the God of heaven. That kingdom shall never be destroyed. And the kingdom shall not be left to other people. But it shall break in pieces and consume (end) all these kingdoms. And it shall stand for ever.

You saw that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands. It brake (broke) in pieces the iron, the brass (bronze), and the clay. It broke the silver, and the gold. The great God has made known to the king what shall happen. And the dream is certain, and the interpretation (meaning) of it sure.
Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, and worshipped Daniel. And he commanded that they should offer an oblation (offering) and sweet odours (incense) to him.
The king answered to Daniel, and said: Of a truth (it is true), your God is a God of gods. He is a Lord of kings, and a revealer (shower) of secrets. For you could reveal this secret.

Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great gifts. He made Daniel ruler over the whole province (land) of Babylon. He made Daniel chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon.
Then Daniel requested of the king. And the king set Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs (business) of Babylon. But Daniel sat in the gate (court) of the king.

Verse 30, which was missing, has been restored. V25 keeps the KJV's like the Son of God.

verses.text: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image (statue) of gold. Its height was 60 cubits (about 90 feet), and its breadth 6 cubits (about 9 feet). He set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province (land) of Babylon.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather the princes, the governors, and the captains. He also sent for the judges, the treasurers, and the counsellors (advisers). He sent for the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces. They were to come to the dedication of the image (statue). It was the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
Then all these rulers were gathered together to the dedication of the image (statue). And they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then an herald (announcer) cried aloud: To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages,

Listen for the sound of the cornet (horn), flute, harp, and sackbut (another kind of harp). Listen for the psaltery (stringed instrument), dulcimer (bagpipe), and all kinds of musick. At that time you must fall down and worship the golden image (statue). It is the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up.
And whoever falls not down and worships shall be cast (thrown) into a furnace. The same hour that person shall be thrown into a burning fiery furnace.

Therefore at that time all the people heard the sound of the musick. Then all the people, the nations, and the languages, fell down. They worshipped the golden image (statue) that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
Then at that time certain Chaldeans (wise men of Babylon) came near, and accused the Jews.
They spoke and said to the king Nebuchadnezzar: O king, live for ever.
You, O king, have made a decree (law). Every man that hears the sound of the musick must fall down. He must worship the golden image (statue).
And whoever falls not down and worships must be cast (thrown) into a furnace. That person must be thrown into the middle of a burning fiery furnace.

There are certain Jews whom you have set over the affairs (business) of Babylon. They are Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, have not regarded (obeyed) you. They serve not your gods. Nor do they worship the golden image (statue) which you have set up.
Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury commanded to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Then they brought these men before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said to them: Is it true, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego? Do not you serve my gods? Do you not worship the golden image (statue) which I have set up?

Now be ready when you hear the sound of the musick. Then fall down and worship the image (statue) which I have made. That will be well. But if you worship not, you shall be cast (thrown) into a furnace. The same hour you shall be thrown into a burning fiery furnace. And who is that God that shall deliver (rescue) you out of my hands?
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered and said to the king: O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful (worried) to answer you in this matter.
If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver (rescue) us. He can rescue us from the burning fiery furnace. And He will deliver (rescue) us out of your hand, O king.
But if not, be it known to you, O king. We will not serve your gods. Nor will we worship the golden image (statue) which you have set up.

Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury. The form of his visage (face) was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Therefore he spoke, and commanded them to heat the furnace. It was to be 7 times hotter than it was wont (usually) to be heated.
And he commanded the most mighty men that were in his army. They were to bind (tie up) Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Then they were to cast (throw) them into the burning fiery furnace.

Then these men were bound in their coats, their hosen (leggings), and their hats. They were bound in their other garments (clothes). And they were cast (thrown) into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
The king's commandment was urgent, and the furnace exceeding (very) hot. Therefore the flame of the fire slew (killed) those men. It killed the men that took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
And these 3 men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound (tied up). They fell into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied (astonished), and rose up in haste (a hurry). He spoke and said to his counsellors (advisers): Did not we cast (throw) 3 men bound (tied up) into the fire? They answered and said to the king: True, O king.
He answered and said: Lo (look), I see 4 men loose (untied). They are walking in the middle of the fire, and they have no hurt. And the form of the fourth is like the Son of God.

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace, and spoke. He said: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you servants of the most high God! Come forth (out), and come here. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came forth (out) of the middle of the fire.

And the princes, governors, and captains were gathered together. The king's counsellors (advisers) were there too, and they saw these men. The fire had no power upon their bodies. Nor was an hair of their head singed (burned). Neither were their coats changed, nor had the smell of fire passed on them.

Then Nebuchadnezzar spoke, and said: Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He has sent His angel, and delivered (rescued) His servants that trusted in Him. They have changed the king's word, and yielded (gave up) their bodies. They would not serve nor worship any god, except their own God.

Therefore I make a decree (law) for every people, nation, and language. Some may speak any thing amiss (wrong) against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Those people shall be cut in pieces. And their houses shall be made a dunghill (garbage heap). For there is no other God that can deliver (rescue) after this sort (in this way).
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, in the province of Babylon.

4.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew/Aramaic, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words. Verses 20-37 (the meaning of the dream, Nebuchadnezzar's 7 years among the beasts, and his praise of God), which were missing, have been restored.

verses.text: Nebuchadnezzar the king writes to all people, nations, and languages. He writes to all that dwell (live) in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.
I thought it good to show the signs and wonders of the high God. He has wrought (done) them toward me.
How great are His signs! And how mighty are His wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. And His dominion (rule) is from generation to generation.
I Nebuchadnezzar was at rest in my house, and flourishing (doing well) in my palace.
I saw a dream which made me afraid. And the thoughts upon my bed and the visions of my head troubled me.
Therefore I made a decree (law) to bring in all the wise men of Babylon. They were to make known to me the interpretation (meaning) of the dream.

Then came in the magicians, the astrologers, the Chaldeans (wise men of Babylon), and the soothsayers (fortune tellers). And I told the dream before them. But they did not make known to me the interpretation (meaning) of it.
But at the last Daniel came in before me. His name was Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god. And in him is the spirit of the holy gods. And before him I told the dream, saying:

O Belteshazzar, master of the magicians! I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you. And no secret troubles you. Tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen. Tell me the interpretation (meaning) of it.
Thus were the visions of my head in my bed: I saw, and look, a tree in the middle of the earth. And the height of it was great.
The tree grew, and was strong. And the height of it reached to heaven. And the sight of it reached to the end of all the earth.

The leaves of it were fair (beautiful), and the fruit of it much. And in it was meat (food) for all. The beasts (animals) of the field had shadow under it. And the fowls (birds) of the heaven dwelt (lived) in the boughs (branches) of it. And all flesh (living things) was fed of it.
I saw in the visions of my head upon my bed. And look, a watcher and an holy one (an angel) came down from heaven.

He cried aloud, and said this: Hew down (cut down) the tree, and cut off his branches. Shake off his leaves, and scatter his fruit. Let the beasts (animals) get away from under it, and the fowls (birds) from his branches.

Nevertheless (but) leave the stump of his roots in the earth. Leave it with a band of iron and brass (bronze). Leave it in the tender grass of the field. And let it be wet with the dew of heaven. And let his portion be with the beasts (animals) in the grass of the earth.
Let his heart be changed from man's. And let a beast's (animal's) heart be given to him. And let 7 times (years) pass over him.

This matter is by the decree (law) of the watchers. The demand is by the word of the holy ones. It is so that the living may know this: the most High rules in the kingdom of men. He gives it to whomever He will. And He sets up over it the basest (lowest) of men.

This dream I king Nebuchadnezzar have seen. Now you, O Belteshazzar, declare (tell) the interpretation (meaning) of it. The wise men of my kingdom are not able to make it known. But you are able, for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was astonied (astonished) for one hour. His thoughts troubled him. The king spoke, and said: Belteshazzar, let not the dream trouble you. Let not the interpretation (meaning) of it trouble you. Belteshazzar answered and said: My lord, the dream be to those who hate you. And the interpretation (meaning) of it be to your enemies.
The tree that you saw grew, and was strong. Its height reached to the heaven. And the sight of it reached to all the earth.

Its leaves were fair (beautiful), and the fruit of it much. And in it was meat (food) for all. Under it the beasts (animals) of the field dwelt (lived). And upon its branches the fowls (birds) of the heaven had their habitation (home).
It is you, O king, that are grown and become strong. For your greatness is grown, and reaches to heaven. And your dominion (rule) reaches to the end of the earth.

And the king saw a watcher and an holy one (an angel) coming down from heaven. He said: Hew the tree down (cut it down), and destroy it. Yet leave the stump of the roots of it in the earth. Leave it with a band of iron and brass (bronze), in the tender grass. And let it be wet with the dew of heaven. Let his portion be with the beasts (animals) of the field. Let it be so till 7 times (years) pass over him.
This is the interpretation (meaning), O king. And this is the decree (law) of the most High. It is come upon my lord the king:

They shall drive you from men. And your dwelling shall be with the beasts (animals) of the field. They shall make you to eat grass as oxen. And they shall wet you with the dew of heaven. And 7 times (years) shall pass over you. Then you will know that the most High rules in the kingdom of men. And He gives it to whomever He will.
And they commanded to leave the stump of the tree roots. So your kingdom shall be sure (kept) to you. That will be after you know that the heavens do rule.

Therefore, O king, let my counsel (advice) be acceptable to you. Break off your sins by righteousness. Break off your iniquities (sins) by showing mercy to the poor. It may be a lengthening of your tranquillity (peace).
All this came upon the king Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of 12 months the king walked in the palace of Babylon.
The king spoke, and said: Is not this great Babylon, that I have built? I built it for the house of the kingdom. I built it by the might of my power. I built it for the honour of my majesty.
The word was still in the king's mouth. Then there fell a voice from heaven, saying: O king Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken. The kingdom is departed (taken) from you.

And they shall drive you from men. Your dwelling shall be with the beasts (animals) of the field. They shall make you to eat grass as oxen. And 7 times (years) shall pass over you. Then you will know that the most High rules in the kingdom of men. And He gives it to whomever He will.

The same hour was the thing fulfilled (done) upon Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen. And his body was wet with the dew of heaven. At last his hairs were grown like eagles' feathers. And his nails were like birds' claws.

At the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up my eyes to heaven. And my understanding returned to me. And I blessed the most High. I praised and honoured Him that lives for ever. His dominion (rule) is an everlasting dominion. And His kingdom is from generation to generation.

And all the inhabitants (people) of the earth are reputed (counted) as nothing. He does according to His will in the army of heaven. He does it among the inhabitants (people) of the earth. And none can stay (stop) His hand, or say to Him: What do You do?

At the same time my reason returned to me. For the glory of my kingdom, my honour and brightness returned to me. And my counsellors (advisers) and my lords sought (came to) me. And I was established (set back) in my kingdom. And excellent majesty was added to me.
Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol (lift up) and honour the King of heaven. All His works are truth, and His ways judgment (justice). And those who walk in pride He is able to abase (bring low).

V25-28 keep the KJV's MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.

verses.text: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to 1,000 of his lords. And he drank wine before the 1,000.

Belshazzar tasted the wine. Then he commanded them to bring the golden and silver vessels (cups). His father Nebuchadnezzar had taken them out of the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted to drink in them with his princes. His wives and his concubines (second wives) would drink in them too.

Then they brought the golden vessels (cups). They were taken out of the temple of the house of God in Jerusalem. And the king and his princes drank in them. His wives and his concubines (second wives) drank in them too.
They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver. They praised gods of brass (bronze), of iron, of wood, and of stone.

In the same hour came forth (out) fingers of a man's hand. They wrote across from the candlestick (lamp stand). They wrote upon the plaister (plaster) of the wall of the king's palace. And the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
Then the king's countenance (face) was changed, and his thoughts troubled him. So the joints of his loins (hips) were loosed. And his knees smote (knocked) one against another.

The king cried aloud to bring in the astrologers. He called the Chaldeans (wise men of Babylon), and the soothsayers (fortune tellers). And the king spoke to the wise men of Babylon: Whoever shall read this writing shall be clothed with scarlet (red). That person must show me the interpretation (meaning). And he shall have a chain of gold about his neck. And he shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Then came in all the king's wise men. But they could not read the writing. Nor could they make known to the king the interpretation (meaning) of it.
Then was king Belshazzar greatly troubled, and his countenance (face) was changed in him. And his lords were astonied (astonished).

Now the queen heard the words of the king and his lords. So she came into the banquet house. And the queen spoke and said: O king, live for ever. Let not your thoughts trouble you. Nor let your countenance (face) be changed.

There is a man in your kingdom. In him is the spirit of the holy gods. In the days of your father, light and understanding were found in him. Wisdom like the wisdom of the gods was found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar your father made him master of the magicians. He was master of the astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers (fortune tellers). I say, the king your father did this.

An excellent spirit was found in the same Daniel. Knowledge and understanding were found in him. He can interpret dreams, and show hard sentences (riddles). He can dissolve doubts (solve hard problems). The king named him Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will show the interpretation (meaning).

Then was Daniel brought in before the king. And the king spoke and said to Daniel: Are you that Daniel? Are you of the children of the captivity (captives) of Judah? Are you the one whom the king my father brought out of Judah?
I have even heard of you. The spirit of the gods is in you. Light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in you.

And now the wise men, the astrologers, have been brought in before me. They were to read this writing. They were to make known to me the interpretation (meaning) of it. But they could not show the interpretation of the thing.

And I have heard of you. You can make interpretations, and dissolve doubts (solve hard problems). Now you may read the writing, and make known its interpretation (meaning). Then you shall be clothed with scarlet (red). You shall have a chain of gold about your neck. And you shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.

Then Daniel answered and said before the king: Let your gifts be to yourself. Give your rewards to another. Yet I will read the writing to the king. I will make known to him the interpretation (meaning).
O king, the most high God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father a kingdom. He gave him majesty, and glory, and honour.

God gave him great majesty. So all people, nations, and languages, trembled (shook) and feared before him. Whom he would he slew (killed), and whom he would he kept alive. And whom he would he set up, and whom he would he put down.
But his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride. Then he was deposed (removed) from his kingly throne. And they took his glory from him.

He was driven from the sons of men. His heart was made like the beasts (animals). His dwelling was with the wild asses (donkeys). They fed him with grass like oxen. And his body was wet with the dew of heaven. This lasted till he knew this: the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men. And God appoints over it whomever He will.
And you his son, O Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart. And you knew all this.

But you have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven. And they have brought the vessels (cups) of His house before you. You and your lords have drunk wine in them. Your wives and your concubines (second wives) have drunk in them too. You have praised the gods of silver, and gold. You praised gods of brass (bronze), iron, wood, and stone. These gods see not, nor hear, nor know. Your breath is in God's hand, and all your ways are His. But this God you have not glorified.
Then was the part of the hand sent from Him. And this writing was written.
And this is the writing that was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
This is the interpretation (meaning) of the thing: MENE (numbered); God has numbered (counted) your kingdom, and finished it.
TEKEL (weighed); You are weighed in the balances (scales), and are found wanting (not good enough).
PERES (divided); Your kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.

Then Belshazzar commanded, and they clothed Daniel with scarlet (red). And they put a chain of gold about his neck. And they made a proclamation (announcement) concerning him. He would be the third ruler in the kingdom.
In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain (killed).
And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about 62 years old.

6.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew/Aramaic, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words.

verses.text: It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom 120 princes (rulers). They should be over the whole kingdom.
And over these princes he set 3 presidents (top officials). Daniel was first of them. The princes were to give accounts (reports) to them. That way the king should have no damage (loss).
Then this Daniel was preferred (honored) above the presidents and princes. It was because an excellent spirit was in him. And the king thought to set him over the whole realm (kingdom).

Then the presidents and princes sought (tried) to find occasion (a reason to accuse) against Daniel. They looked in his work for the kingdom. But they could find no occasion nor fault. For he was faithful. There was not any error or fault found in him.
Then said these men: We shall not find any occasion (reason to accuse) against this Daniel. We will only find it against him concerning the law of his God.
Then these presidents and princes assembled together (came all together) to the king. And they said this to him: King Darius, live for ever.

All the presidents of the kingdom have consulted together. The governors and the princes did too, with the counsellors (advisers) and the captains. They want to establish a royal statute (law). They want to make a firm decree (law). For 30 days, no one may ask a petition (prayer) of any God or man. They may only ask you, O king. Whoever does shall be cast (thrown) into the den of lions.
Now, O king, establish the decree (law), and sign the writing. Then it may not be changed. Make it by the law of the Medes and Persians, which alters (changes) not.
So king Darius signed the writing and the decree (law).

Now Daniel knew that the writing was signed. Then he went into his house. His windows were open in his chamber (room) toward Jerusalem. He kneeled upon his knees 3 times a day. He prayed, and gave thanks before his God. He did it as he did before.
Then these men assembled (came all together). They found Daniel praying and making supplication (asking for help) before his God.

Then they came near, and spoke before the king concerning the king's decree (law): Have you not signed a decree? It says: For 30 days no one may ask a petition (prayer) of God or man. Only you, O king, may be asked. Whoever does shall be cast (thrown) into the den of lions. The king answered and said: The thing is true. It is the law of the Medes and Persians, which alters (changes) not.

Then they answered and said before the king: Daniel is of the children of the captivity (captives) of Judah. He regards (obeys) not you, O king. Nor does he obey the decree (law) that you have signed. But he makes his petition (prayer) 3 times a day.

Then the king heard these words, and was sore displeased (very upset) with himself. And he set his heart on Daniel to deliver (rescue) him. He laboured (worked hard) till the going down of the sun to rescue him.
Then these men assembled (came all together) to the king, and said to the king: Know, O king, the law of the Medes and Persians. No decree (law) nor statute which the king establishes may be changed.

Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel. They cast (threw) him into the den of lions. Now the king spoke and said to Daniel: Your God whom you serve continually, He will deliver (rescue) you.

And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den. And the king sealed it with his own signet (seal ring). He sealed it with the signet of his lords too. That way the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting (without food). Neither were instruments of musick brought before him. And his sleep went from him.
Then the king arose (got up) very early in the morning. He went in haste (a hurry) to the den of lions.

And he came to the den. Then he cried with a lamentable (sad) voice to Daniel. And the king spoke and said to Daniel: O Daniel, servant of the living God! You serve your God continually. Is He able to deliver (rescue) you from the lions?
Then said Daniel to the king: O king, live for ever.
My God has sent His angel, and has shut the lions' mouths. So the lions have not hurt me. For before Him innocency (innocence) was found in me. And also before you, O king, have I done no hurt.

Then was the king exceeding (very) glad for him. He commanded them to take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den. And no manner of hurt was found upon him. It was because he believed in his God.

And the king commanded, and they brought those men which had accused Daniel. They cast (threw) them into the den of lions. They threw them, their children, and their wives. And the lions had the mastery of them. The lions brake (broke) all their bones in pieces. They did it before the men came at the bottom of the den.
Then king Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages. He wrote to all that dwell (live) in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.

I make a decree (law) for every dominion (land) of my kingdom. Men must tremble (shake) and fear before the God of Daniel. For He is the living God, and stedfast (lasting) for ever. His kingdom is that which shall not be destroyed. And His dominion (rule) shall be even to the end.
He delivers (rescues) and rescues. He works signs and wonders in heaven and in earth. He has delivered (rescued) Daniel from the power of the lions.
So this Daniel prospered (did well) in the reign of Darius. He also prospered in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
